title: Aviation Black Box for AI: Technical Design of an Immutable Deployment Log

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a logging standard specification enables incident investigation, but the path from a design document to adopted infrastructure is long.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: designing tamper-resistant immutable logging systems requires systems engineering and security knowledge beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: specifying data categories, tamper-resistance mechanisms, and investigation protocols requires thorough systems design work.

novelty.reasoning: Largely addressed: multiple open-source implementations (AIR, Unworldly, AgentLens) already provide tamper-evident flight recorder functionality for AI systems.

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multiple open-source implementations already exist. 'AIR' (air-blackbox-gateway) is an OpenAI-compatible reverse proxy that records every LLM call with HMAC-SHA256 tamper-evident audit chains, explicitly modeled as a 'flight recorder for AI systems'. 'Unworldly' provides tamper-proof, ISO 42001 + HIPAA-compliant audit trails with SHA-256 hash chains. 'AgentLens' captures every LLM call, tool invocation, and approval decision. These tools are featured on Hacker News and GitHub. Additionally, blockchain-based approaches for immutable AI audit trails have been published in MDPI journals. The concept of WORM storage for AI logs is well-established in compliance literature. The core design work this idea proposes is substantially implemented in existing tools.
